topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text: I've not seen him in the fields, nor at the well. They say he's been scribbling, filling pages with words about her, about us, the village, the very fields we sow. I've heard whispers, how the pages speak of our days, our nights, more than we know or wish to know. What if these words find their way to wrong hands, or minds that twist the truth like weeds pull at the roots? What if the tales he weaves change how we're seen, or what we hold dear? I pray to Saint Benedict, guardian of the countryside, protector of our peace, that these words be as harmless as the clouds that drift over our valley, leaving only gentle rains and not the storms that strike the soul.
